name: Ward rota
summary: Nurses cover a ward around the clock in fixed shifts, with a minimum number on duty at every hour and a guaranteed rest between shifts.
when_to_choose: Choose this if you staff one or more wards twenty-four hours a day, the shifts are the same length every day, and the hard part is making sure enough people are on at night without anyone working back to back.

knobs.label: Days in the rota cycle
knobs.help: How long the pattern runs before it repeats. Fourteen days is the usual choice; a longer cycle gives fairer weekends but is harder to read.

knobs.label: Shift length
knobs.help: Twelve hours means two shifts a day and one handover. Eight means three shifts a day and three handovers.

knobs.label: Minimum nurses on each shift
knobs.help: The number that must be on the ward at all times during a shift, including at night.

knobs.label: Rest between shifts
knobs.help: In hours. The gap a nurse must have after finishing one shift before starting the next.

questions: How many wards are you rostering, and how many nurses belong to each?
Do you run two twelve-hour shifts a day, or three shorter ones?
How many nurses must be on the ward at the quietest time of the night?
How much rest do you give between the end of one shift and the start of the next?
Are there nurses who only work days, only nights, or only certain days of the week?
tradeoffs: Twelve-hour shifts mean one handover a day and more whole days off in a row, but the days are long and a night is hard to recover from; eight-hour shifts spread the load and suit part-time staff, at the cost of needing more people on the rota and handing over three times a day.

A longer rest between shifts protects staff but makes a short cycle difficult to fill: with eleven hours' rest and twelve-hour shifts, nobody can work an evening and the next morning, so the cycle needs enough people to cover both.
Setting the night minimum equal to the day minimum is safest but is usually what makes a rota impossible; most wards run one fewer at night and accept that a busy night has less slack.
